speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly when the pain occurs and how long it lasts?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the shooting pain triggered by chewing and your history of recurrent ear infections, are you experiencing any pain, fullness, or tinnitus when you swallow or yawn?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That shooting pain while chewing is a classic sign of tensor tympani spasm or myofascial pain, but it could also be referred pain from a TMJ issue or a neuroma. When you wear an earring, do the earrings touch the inner ear canal or sit directly against the outer ear cartilage where your surgery was?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auricular Chondritis (infection of the auricular cartilage following tympanoplasty). The history of recurrent ear infections, shooting pain, and the specific context of recent cartilage surgery suggests a superinfection of the external ear cartilage rather than a TMJ or neuroma issue.
